semantic_correction.stem: A client with diabetes lives far from the clinic and has missed several in-person diabetes self-management education visits because of transportation problems. Which care-planning action is most appropriate?

options.A: Offer a telehealth or digital DSMES option that fits the client’s needs and preferences, while continuing in-person clinical care when it is needed.
options.B: Send general online diabetes handouts and close the DSMES referral, using the same materials regardless of the client’s learning needs or preferences.
options.C: Move diabetes education and medical follow-up to telehealth as the standard plan, including visits that would otherwise require an in-person examination.
options.D: Postpone further DSMES until reliable transportation is arranged, and use routine clinic follow-up to address self-management questions in the meantime.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 American Diabetes Association Standards of Care recommend offering DSMES through telehealth and/or digital interventions to meet individual preferences, reduce access barriers, and improve satisfaction. The same Standards discuss transportation and geographic access as barriers that can be mitigated through creative delivery options such as telehealth and online services. ADA Section 1 also states that telehealth should complement rather than universally replace in-person care for optimal diabetes management. Therefore A most directly addresses the transportation barrier while preserving individualized in-person clinical care when needed. B uses digital material but abandons individualized DSMES and ignores learning needs and preferences. C overextends telehealth into a default substitute for visits that may require an in-person examination. D leaves the access barrier unresolved and delays an evidence-supported DSMES delivery option.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Use telehealth or digital DSMES to reduce access barriers when appropriate to the client’s needs and preferences while preserving in-person clinical care when clinically necessary.
semantic_correction.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes
semantic_correction.source_document_title: 5. Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026; 1. Improving Care and Promoting Health in Populations: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Diabetes Care 2026;49(Supplement 1); published December 8, 2025; primary articles rechecked August 20, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Section 5 Recommendation 5.6: offer DSMES via telehealth and/or digital interventions to meet individual preferences, reduce access barriers, and improve satisfaction. Recommendation 5.5 and supporting text preserve person-centered DSMES responsive to individual preferences and needs. Supporting text identifies geographic location, technology access, transportation challenges, accessibility, and timing as access considerations and describes telehealth/online delivery as options to mitigate barriers. Section 1, Flexible Modalities of Care Delivery: telehealth can improve access to diabetes care and DSMES but should complement and not replace in-person visits for optimal glycemic management.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: Current ADA standards support individualized telehealth/digital DSMES to reduce access barriers and meet preferences, while telehealth complements rather than universally replaces clinically needed in-person diabetes care.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.7 (official PDF pageno 10): identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members; assess the need for referrals and obtain necessary orders; initiate, evaluate and update the client plan of care; recognize limitations and utilize resources; utilize resources to promote quality client care, including information technology. Detailed Referrals, printed p.22 (official PDF pageno 25): assess the need to refer clients for assistance with existing or potential problems; assess need for referrals and obtain necessary orders; identify community resources.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup retained the telehealth-DSMES access construct, removed the old absolute/complete-replacement cues, balanced A/B/C/D length, and after GitHub reread revised B to eliminate a second-answer risk from potentially legitimate self-directed digital DSMES.

scope_exclusions.universal_telehealth: The item does not claim telehealth is appropriate for every client or every diabetes encounter.
scope_exclusions.replacement_of_examination: Telehealth DSMES is not presented as a substitute for physical examination or other in-person care when clinically needed.
scope_exclusions.technology_access: The key assumes that a suitable telehealth or digital option can be offered after considering the client’s needs and preferences; it does not assume every client has adequate connectivity or digital literacy.
scope_exclusions.payer_rules: No insurance, reimbursement, licensure-jurisdiction, or telehealth billing requirement is tested.
scope_exclusions.specific_platform: No particular app, video platform, device, or vendor is endorsed.
scope_exclusions.clinical_treatment: The item tests access to DSMES rather than remote diagnosis, medication titration, or management of an acute complication.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for ‘telehealth digital DSMES transportation access barriers’ returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank scan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It directly addresses the stated transportation barrier using an ADA-supported individualized delivery option while preserving clinically necessary in-person care.
option_audit.B: Plausible because online materials can reinforce diabetes education, but closing the DSMES referral and using generic materials irrespective of individual needs does not meet person-centered DSMES guidance.
option_audit.C: Plausible because telehealth can support both education and clinical care, but it overgeneralizes remote delivery to visits that may require in-person examination.
option_audit.D: Plausible because transportation assistance can be useful, but postponing DSMES leaves a current barrier unresolved despite an evidence-supported remote option.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer after correction. A directly resolves the access barrier while preserving individualized DSMES and the proper boundary of telehealth. B is generic and terminates individualized DSMES, C overextends telehealth beyond appropriate scope, and D delays accessible education rather than using a recommended alternative delivery method.

cueing_check.note: The key is the shortest by only two characters; all four options are care-planning actions of comparable length and none relies on only/all/always/never/every cueing.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: NCSBN explicitly includes referral assessment, multidisciplinary collaboration, plan-of-care updating, resource use, and information technology within Management of Care, supporting an entry-level RN decision about removing an access barrier to an education/referral service.
